open_points.subject: attempt_number ownership (A11)
open_points.text: "A10 and A11: ... EffectAttempts and attempt numbers ..." (effects owns) / "`store` alone assigns `attempt_number`, inside the transaction that writes the record ... no caller passes a number, `effects` included."
open_points.question: Which module is the primary owner of the attempt-number rule and its invariants (ordinal assignment, next-ordinal check, refusal when not next)?
options: `store` owns all attempt-number semantics and enforcement; `effects` only triggers writes
`effects` owns attempt-number semantics; `store` only provides a primitive counter/position
open_points.default_guess: `store` is the owner of numbering and enforcement, with `effects` owning only lifecycle sequencing around sends.

open_points.subject: unknown-reference refusal sequencing
open_points.text: "It gives the 'unknown reference' refusal ..." (surface) / "Must not own ... Any operation's own checks or records" (surface) / A16 rule 1 requires unknown reference before record-own checks
open_points.question: Who performs existence checks that drive the uniform unknown-reference refusal: `surface` generically, or each owning module as its first domain check?
options: `surface` queries existence directly (likely via `store`) before dispatching operation logic
Owning modules perform first existence checks and return a typed missing-reference outcome that `surface` maps to the uniform refusal
open_points.default_guess: Owning modules detect missing references first; `surface` normalizes the refusal.

open_points.subject: configuration path from command-line argument
open_points.text: A17 rule 1: "The kernel reads the file's path from its one command-line argument ..."; State 3 defines `surface.serve_kernel` start order beginning at `installation.load_installation` but assigns no module to argv intake.
open_points.question: Which module owns reading/validating the single CLI argument and passing the path into startup?
open_points.default_guess: Bootstrap/`surface` reads argv and passes the path into `installation`.
